title: Addresses and sizes
description:
Print where variables live and how big they are.

```
char    c at 0x7ffd5c1e2a17, 1 byte
int     i at 0x7ffd5c1e2a18, 4 bytes
double  d at 0x7ffd5c1e2a20, 8 bytes
int*    p at 0x7ffd5c1e2a28, 8 bytes, holds 0x7ffd5c1e2a18
*p = 42
```
hints: A `char*` printed with `<<` is treated as text, which is why the cast to `const void*` is needed (lesson 1.02).
requirements: Four local variables; print each address with `static_cast<const void*>(&x)` and `sizeof`.
`p` points at `i`; print what it holds and what `*p` reads.
stretch: Print the addresses of the elements of an `int[4]` and the distance between them.
